newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money trade largely steady.
newsitem.headline: German call money trade largely steady.

text.p: German overnight funds again traded mostly steady around three percent Tuesday as liquidity conditions still appeared ample with dealers predicting the Bundesbank would refrain from making an adjustment this week.

Like on Monday, the bulk of short-term funds changed hands at around three percent. "Call money is being offered (rather than demanded) today and while the bulk of trades is being conducted at around three percent, there have been some trades near 2.95 percent. So rates should probably continue to trade between 2.98 percent and 3.01 percent," a dealer said.
Dealers said they expected the month-end to be slightly more relaxed in July after rates had tended to gyrate a bit more strongly at the end of the month in recent months.
In light of still ample liquidity conditions, dealers did not expect the Bundesbank to add much in terms extra liquidity when the 77.9 billion mark repo pact expires on Wednesday.
Banks held 41.0 billion marks in reserve on Monday after 41.8 billion marks on Friday while the average rate continued to be at 41.1 billion marks. Lombard borrowings stood at 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average as set at 3.01667 percent on Tuesday after Montag 3.02675 percent on Monday.
